title: OpenAI Responses mapping: stream-event reconciliation and structured-output guardrails
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Background: As we onboard third-party models and implement an OpenAI Responses compatibility layer, we see subtle but production-impacting differences in streaming event shapes, tool-call semantics, and structured output embedding. These differences surface as: (1) truncated or duplicated token events during streaming when our runtime merges partial deltas, (2) mismatched tool invocation payloads between a "responses" style tool_call event and our existing function-calling API, and (3) structured JSON outputs that lose schema markers when events are split across multiple stream frames.

Objective: Audit and remediate the mapping ambiguities so that the Redwood Responses shim can: (a)emit a deterministic stream sequence that downstream SDKs and customers expect, (b) preserve structured-output boundaries and schema hints across frames, and (c) provide a robust fallback/failure policy for tool/function calls that mirrors OpenAI semantics (including name resolution, arguments types, and tool-level errors).

Scope: This ticket covers runtime-level mapping logic, tests (unit + end-to-end), and a conservative adapter implemented in the runtime translation layer. It excludes UX changes in Console and long-term protocol redesign (that will be a separate RFC).

Non-goals: Full feature parity for edge-case signals (e.g., experimental "editor_state" fields) and language-specific SDK shims beyond Node/Python minimal expectations.

Proposed approach: 1) Create a canonical "responses event model" translator that normalizes incoming stream frames into an internal event sequence, preserving three attributes: event_type, canonical_token_delta, and structured_boundary_id. 2) Implement a micro-buffer that merges deltas only when it is safe to do so (based on UTF-8 boundary detection and JSON bracket/quote balance heuristics). 3) Add a tool-call reconciliation layer that maps our function-calling contract to Responses tool_call semantics with explicit conversion rules for argument encoding (json-string vs native map) and error bubbling. 4) Provide runtime flags to opt into strict vs permissive mapping during rollout and add a canary route for affected customers.
acceptance_criteria: Automated unit tests that validate streaming reconstructions for at least 6 canonical split cases (emoji/UTF8 splits, partial JSON chunks, nested braces across frames)
End-to-end integration tests using the responses-interop test harness that assert structured-output JSON is parseable after stream reassembly
Tool-call mapping implementation with documented conversion table and 3+ sample contracts (sync tool success, tool error with stack, tool not-found fallback)
A canary rollout config and telemetry instrumentation for mismatched-event rate and tool-call failures
Documentation added to internal Confluence page describing fallbacks and SDK expectations
updates: 2026-02-25 - Kickoff: scoped ticket, identified UTF-8 and JSON-fragmentation as highest-risk sources of structured-output loss
2026-02-28 - Spike: built a small harness (tests/stream-reconstruct) that demonstrates duplication when runtime merges overlapping deltas; confirmed behavior with model X v3.1

2026-03-03 - Design review: decided on bracket/quote balance heuristics plus byte-boundary safety check rather than heavyweight parse attempts on every frame (tradeoff: simpler and faster, risk: pathological inputs may still split within escapes)
2026-03-05 - Experiment: micro-buffer implementation reduced parse errors by ~82% on fixture corpus (n=4500 simulated streams)
2026-03-08 - Security consult: confirmed tool-call mapping needs strict validation of argument serialization; flagged for security review (ticket flagged on release branch)
2026-03-10 - Implementation progress: core translator implemented behind feature-flag, added early telemetry for malformed-frame-rate; starting integration tests
comments: PM note (Aisha Patel): prioritize customer-facing determinism — failing fast with a clear fallback is preferable to silent data mangling

Design feedback (Jordan Park): suggest including a lightweight schema marker for structured outputs (e.g., "__redwood_struct_id") to make boundary reconstruction more robust — assess privacy/compat implications
Review request (Riley Chen): please verify that the micro-buffer doesn't significantly increase P95 latency for 1-token completion workloads
QA note (Lina Rao): will add fuzz tests for escaped-quote heavy payloads and binary-like base64 blobs in follow-up
